newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BANK SUPPORT BILL SEEN IN FORCE TO 1998.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BANK SUPPORT BILL SEEN IN FORCE TO 1998.

text.p: Parliament's soon four-year old decision guaranteeing unlimited state support to Finnish banks should not be overturned until 1998, the legislature's economic committee said in a statement received on Friday.
It would be possible to evaluate whether the conditions existed to cancel the decision only after planned legislation to put a cap on state guarantees for bank deposits had taken force, it said.
The act to limit state protection of bank deposits was expected to take effect at the start of 1998, it added. The plan is to guarantee deposits up to 150,000 markka.
Parliament unlimited bank support decision, made in February 1993 when the banking sector crisis of the early 1990s was still escalating, says:

"Parliament requires the State of Finland to guarantee that Finnish banks are able to meet their commitments on time under all circumstances. Whenever necessary, Parliament shall grant sufficient appropriations and powers to be used by the Government for meeting such commitments."
The economic committee's statement is parliament's response to a government report on state support to banks, and it will form the base for a plenary debate on Saturday.

Parliament's state finance committee said earlier this week in its statement on the government report that the conditions existed already now to cancel the decision granting unlimited state guarantees to banks.

The economic committee is the parliamentary committee responsible for the banking sector. Its view on when it would be appropriate to consider cancelling the unlimited support decision echoed the opinion voiced by the government in the report.
